intro: The organist begins with the feet alone. Fabian Wöhrle plays Buxtehude’s C-major Praeludium, where that first flourish grows into a fugue and finally a quick dance over a repeating bass.

sections.label: Intro · The pedals begin alone
sections.mNote: Four bars for the feet before the hands join

sections.label: A · The fugue takes up the flourish
sections.mNote: The opening pedal figure becomes a fugue subject

sections.label: Link · Runs above the pedals
sections.mNote: The last fugue entry leads into free running notes

sections.label: B · A three-bar bass keeps returning
sections.mNote: Eight statements of the ground beneath changing upper parts

cues.title: The feet begin alone
cues.text: For four bars the organist plays only with the feet. The pedal line leaps, runs and turns back on itself while both hands wait. The first notes on the keyboards arrive near the end of bar five.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 1–5: pedal solo, with the first manual notes late in bar 5. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Evening music in Lübeck
cues.text: Buxtehude takes up the organist’s post at Lübeck’s Marienkirche in 1668. Alongside the services, he develops the church’s public evening concerts, the Abendmusiken. From 1678 these include sacred dramatic works.
cues.evidence: Marienkirche’s historical account gives the 1668 appointment and the sacred dramatic Abendmusiken from 1678. https://www.st-marien-luebeck.de/en/music/dieterich-buxtehude

cues.title: The flourish becomes a fugue
cues.text: The quick figure from the pedal solo now passes from voice to voice in a fugue. Each new entry has company: the earlier voice keeps playing as the next one begins.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 36–64. Relf Clark connects the fugue subject with bar 2 of the pedal solo. https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Bach overstays his leave
cues.text: In 1705 Bach goes to Lübeck to hear Buxtehude. His employers in Arnstadt grant four weeks’ leave; he stays away for four months. Back at work, he has to explain the absence to the church authorities.
cues.evidence: Marienkirche’s account quotes Bach’s obituary and the Arnstadt consistory minutes of 21 February 1706. https://www.st-marien-luebeck.de/en/music/dieterich-buxtehude

cues.title: The keyboards run free
cues.text: The last fugue entry opens straight into rapid runs on the keyboards. The pedals alternate moving notes with long-held ones; above them, the hands answer one another with scales.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 64–74; Relf Clark identifies the unbroken continuation from the final subject entry. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf ; https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Three bars, eight times
cues.text: Presto Ciacona: a fast dance in triple metre. A three-bar bass pattern returns eight times, while the parts above it change. The little ground grows from the fugue subject, which itself grew from the opening pedal solo.
cues.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), from bar 75, marked Presto Ciacona in 3/2. Relf Clark identifies the eight statements and the ground’s relation to the subject. https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A 1984 organ in Gerstetten
cues.text: Fabian Wöhrle plays the Reiser organ of the Catholic church of St Peter and St Paul in Gerstetten, a town in Baden-Württemberg. Built in 1984, it has two manuals, pedals and 22 stops.
cues.evidence: The Commons description of this recording names the performer, the church and the Reiser organ, II/P/22, 1984 (two manuals, pedal, 22 stops): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:D._Buxtehude_Pr%C3%A4ludium,_Fuge_und_Chaconne_C-Dur_BuxWV_137_Fabian_W%C3%B6hrle_Kath._Kirche_Gerstetten.mp3

transitions.title: The pedal flourish reaches the hands
transitions.to: A · The fugue takes up the flourish
transitions.how: The bass reaches C and the pedals fall silent. A running figure on the keyboards begins the fugue, taking up the shape of the opening pedal solo. Further voices enter one by one; eventually the pedals have the subject again.
transitions.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 35–40. Relf Clark explains the subject’s origin in the pedal solo. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf ; https://www.hyperion-records.co.uk/dw.asp?dc=W10872_GBAJY0861201

transitions.title: The last entry runs onwards
transitions.from: A · The fugue takes up the flourish
transitions.how: The pedals carry the last fugue entry straight into the freer passage. Above them, the right hand spills into a descending scale. Further runs pass between the hands until a long G in the pedals holds the music on the dominant of C.
transitions.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 64–74; Relf Clark identifies the final subject entry at bar 64. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf

transitions.title: G resolves into the dancing bass
transitions.to: B · A three-bar bass keeps returning
transitions.how: The held G prepares C major. At Presto Ciacona, the metre changes to 3/2 and the pedals begin the three-bar ground on C. The hands strike a chord, then leave the bass room to establish its pattern.
transitions.evidence: Les Éditions Outremontaises score (2007), bars 70–77, especially the G pedal and the change to Presto Ciacona at bar 75. https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/2/20/IMSLP126836-WIMA.e9e1-Buxtehude_Praeludium_137.pdf
